title: Numerical Feature Scaling and Normalization
description: Transformation of continuous features onto uniform numerical scales for distance-based and gradient-based algorithms.
conditions: Algorithms sensitive to feature magnitudes (PCA, K-Means, SVM, KNN, Neural Nets)
Features measured in disparate physical units (e.g., Age [0-100] vs Income [10k-500k])
Presence of moderate outliers in continuous features
recommended_methods: StandardScaler (Z-score normalization: zero mean, unit variance)
RobustScaler (Median centering and IQR scaling) for outlier-resilient scaling
selection_rules: If features contain extreme outliers that cannot be capped, select RobustScaler over StandardScaler
If model requires strictly positive bounded features (e.g. image pixels, Naive Bayes), select MinMaxScaler
If model is tree-based (Random Forest, XGBoost), scaling is unnecessary and can be skipped
limitations: MinMaxScaler is completely compromised if unseen test data exceeds training min/max bounds
StandardScaler distorts true sparsity when applied to sparse matrices (use MaxAbsScaler instead)
